niche: an English distribution network operator's DSO planning team forecasting, for its December 2026 capital expenditure review, each constrained 33/11 kV primary's design-day peak for winter 2027/28 with its flexibility contract called in full, expected and at the one-day-in-ten level, from three winters of dispatch and SCADA records in which calls were mostly smaller than the contract
answer: Commit reinforcement at Ashcombe Road, Fenwick Street and Hartwell Common for winter 2027/28; Charlecote Way stays within firm capacity on nine design days in ten
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans every file, leaves the logged switching days out, measures each event against a weather-adjusted baseline, regresses megawatts delivered per megawatt scheduled on temperature zone by zone, applies the minus 3 C rate to the megawatts contracted, takes the credit off the 17:30 to 18:00 peak and carries the megawatts of scatter that fit leaves to the one-day-in-ten level reinforces Hartwell Common alone: it earns the demand before flexibility and its own backtest, and loses the megawatts delivered at the two zones whose cold-day calls stopped short of the contract, Ashcombe Road's peak after the window, every one-day-in-ten level but Hartwell Common's, the bridge and the set.
domain_test: The deciding quantities are a distribution planner's: a primary's design-day peak before flexibility (a weather-corrected peak grown to the winter assessed), what a demand-side flexibility contract delivers in the evening peak when called in full (limited by what the provider's enrolled assets have available on a cold evening, not by what is scheduled), the residual peak once the curtailed load comes back after the service window, and the level that peak stays under on nine design days in ten against N-1 firm capacity; with clinics and locum cover in place of primaries and flexibility nothing is scheduled in megawatts against a contracted registered capacity, nothing comes back after a window, and no half-hourly day shape moves a peak from one half-hour to another.
stakeholder_role: the network operator's head of DSO for the Halverton zone, who takes the winter 2027/28 reinforcement list to the December investment committee

spine.entity: one row is one primary substation's metered demand in one half-hour, as its SCADA export writes it

world.geography: England (a fictional distribution network operator, licence area and city zone)

driver: A contracted intervention is called in units up to a contracted amount, and the record's calls were mostly smaller than the contract and were met; what the intervention can remove shows only on the occasions a call outran it, as a share of the contracted amount that falls with a condition and varies from occasion to occasion in proportion to its level; part of what is removed returns just after the intervention's window and can move the constrained unit's peak there; each of these, and the forecast of the unit's peak before the intervention, is carried to a larger contract called in full under a design condition, as an expected peak and a one-occasion-in-ten level, and checked by predicting the latest period's occasions from the earlier ones.
driver_concrete: Each Halverton zone primary's design-day peak for winter 2027/28 with its flexibility contract scheduled in full: the megawatts delivered at 17:30 to 18:00 are the share of the contracted megawatts the provider has available at minus 3 C (0.39 Corvane Flex, 0.54 Quillon, read from the cold days on which nearly every call outran it, the same at both of a provider's zones and through three winters of growing contracts), not the megawatts delivered per megawatt scheduled that the part calls at Ashcombe Road and Charlecote Way show; the day is rebuilt half-hour by half-hour with the load that comes back after the window, which moves Ashcombe Road's peak to the half-hour ending 20:00 (25.9 MW against 22.0 at 18:00 and firm 23.0); the day-to-day spread of what is available is carried in proportion to the 2027/28 megawatts to the nine-days-in-ten level, which puts Fenwick Street over firm; the approach is back-tested on winter 2025/26 from the two winters before, a test megawatts per megawatt scheduled also passes.
stump: The careful but hurried pass (megawatts delivered per megawatt scheduled regressed on temperature zone by zone, the minus 3 C rate applied to the megawatts contracted, the credit taken off the 17:30 to 18:00 peak, the megawatts of scatter its fit leaves carried unchanged, or the fit's own range) reinforces Hartwell Common alone; the same rate with the scatter carried in proportion reinforces Fenwick Street and Hartwell Common, as does the available share right with the credit off the 17:30 to 18:00 peak and megawatts of scatter unchanged; the megawatts contracted at face value reinforce nothing; the megawatts the 2025/26 contracts made available carried unchanged reinforce all four; the available share right with the expected day set against firm capacity reinforces Ashcombe Road and Hartwell Common; only every result of the chain reinforces Ashcombe Road, Fenwick Street and Hartwell Common.
deep_chain: (1) design-day demand before flexibility on the guideline's days, the weather correction's line checked on cold hours the sample does not hold; (2) the share of its contracted megawatts each provider has available on the design day, from the cold days on which calls outran it; (3) the megawatts each contract delivers; (4) the same model fitted on the two earlier winters set against the last; (5) what comes back after the window; (6) the megawatts off the day's peak and the half-hour that then peaks; (7) the expected peak; (8) the day-to-day spread as a share of what is delivered; (9) the nine-days-in-ten level; (10) the primaries to reinforce; (11) each contract's megawatts bridged to the megawatts off the peak.
judgment: four judgments, each moving figures: megawatts delivered follow the megawatts contracted, not the megawatts scheduled, once a call outruns what is available (settled by the equal-temperature test, the two zones of each provider and three winters of stepped-up contracts; a held-out winter passes both readings); the day's peak is its highest half-hour with the load that comes back (measured on every event, carried to the larger delivery); the spread of what is available scales with its level (the same share at a 3 MW and a 7.5 MW contract) and is carried with the baseline's to one day in ten; the weather correction's straight line is carried past a sample that holds no cold day, on the evidence of the hours before the service window.
one_fact_test: the most useful single sentence (a provider can deliver no more than a share of its contracted megawatts on a cold evening, however many are scheduled) rescues 2 of 11 results (the share and the megawatts delivered); told it, a pass that still takes the credit off the 17:30 to 18:00 peak with the record's megawatts of scatter reinforces Fenwick Street and Hartwell Common; the come-back sentence rescues the come-back rate alone and the spread sentence the spread alone

lineage.architecture: v5 (the same world: each provider's reduction net of the load the control room moved to the primary across an open point, read at minus 3.0 C)
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what a contracted intervention removes from a constrained unit's demand under a design condition, but on every occasion the record measured it the operator also moved part of the unit's load onto a neighbouring unit for the same hours, so the unit's measured reduction is the intervention plus the move and the neighbour, the natural comparison, rose by what was moved; only the intervention's own reduction, read where the move cancels, is credited under the design condition, when the neighbour has no room to take it.
lineage.stump: Measuring each flexibility event's fall at its zone primary against a weather-adjusted baseline, validated on held-out non-event weekdays and stable across both winters, and crediting the 2027/28 contracts at the 0.9, 0.6, 0.9 and 0.9 per megawatt scheduled the event records show commits no primary; the step that lands it there is reading the primary's fall as the provider's delivery, when at Ashcombe Road, Fenwick Street and Hartwell Common the control room moved a feeder section across an open point to Tollbrook Lane, Wexley Hill and Kestwick Fields for each event window, so the providers' own reduction, net of the neighbour's rise and read at the design day's minus 3.0 C, is 0.4 and 0.5 per megawatt and Ashcombe Road and Hartwell Common must be reinforced.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-10 on the platform's holistic audit: both round 2 runs lost at the deciding step (Ashcombe Road alone) and the audit still read the neighbour's flat step on event days as one built-in factor, one subtraction once told, a plant; round 1 had one run on the golden through paired totals

lineage.architecture: v3 (re-root in batch 1: a Victorian local government union branch choosing the councils at which it applies for protected action ballot orders for ballots opening 1 March 2027, a ballot counting only if half the roll votes, each member's vote carried from the branch's own online votes and lifted where an elected workplace delegate is active at the member's worksite)
lineage.driver: Each unit's chance of acting in a coming event is carried from its own record of past acts and lifted where a contact a separate dated register places at its site is in post, and the register's contacts changed after the last past act the record holds, so every route carried on the units' own record, each of which reproduces the last closed event, brings the old contacts into the coming event.
lineage.driver_concrete: A member's chance of voting in a protected action ballot rises about 24 points where an elected delegate is active at their worksite, read from the branch's delegate register terms against each member's worksite on the roll; the July 2026 delegate elections, held after the last online vote in October 2025, left worksites at some councils with no delegate and filled others, so turnout carried from members' own votes over-forecasts the councils that lost delegates and under-forecasts those that gained them.
lineage.stump: Carrying each member's own voting history, calibrated to the 2021 and 2023-24 declared turnouts and checked on the 2023-24 round within a point, files 15 councils above half; the step that lands it there is reading each member's past votes as theirs alone when they rode the elected delegate in post at their worksite at the time, and the July 2026 delegate elections left worksites at six of those councils without one and filled worksites at two others, so with the 2026-28 delegates the set is 11.
lineage.fate: FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal (2026-11-07): both responses landed the 11 councils; each put worksite delegate coverage in its member-level turnout logit from the start and evaluated it at the ballot close with the 2026-28 delegates, so the decisive step was a recorded covariate's forward value one join from the members' worksite code, and the July 2026 election return, read by nothing else, announced it; driver spent

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how often a fixed capacity is exceeded once a steady load is added, when both the standing load and the response each driving event adds scale with how much of a fixed network lies below a fluctuating level read from a separate record, so one response and one standing load read off a short record whose level mostly stayed low understate a long record whose level often rose past most of the network.
lineage.stump: Fitting one unit-hydrograph response per millimetre and the meter's own dry weather flow on 2024 to 2026 and replaying 2004 to 2023 files about 1 overflow a year with the subdivision (0.70), inside the consent's two, and connects it; the step that lands it there is reading the station's response as fixed when its infiltration rises 4.2 L/s for every kilometre of sewer below the water table, which stood a median 0.2 km over the meter and 2.1 km over the replay.
lineage.driver_concrete: The infiltration reaching the pump station on a dry day and in a storm scales with the length of the catchment's sewers whose inverts lie below the water table that day, read from the regional bore's level against the asset register's invert levels; the 2024 to 2026 meter ran through years when the water table mostly stood below the low terrace's sewers, while the consent's 2004 to 2023 replay holds wet years with it above most of them, so one response per millimetre and the meter's base flow carried into the replay understate the overflows the subdivision's added flow takes past the consent.
lineage.architecture: v2 (re-root in batch 1: a New Zealand district council's wastewater pump station, whether a subdivision can connect in 2027 within the station's consented overflows, the infiltration each storm and each dry day drives read from the length of sewer below the water table)
lineage.fate: FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal (2026-11-07): both responses landed the hold call; Response 1 replayed 2004 to 2023 and filed 48 overflows against the 40 allowed, then 2 after the upgrade, so any full-record replay with the subdivision already broke the consent and the water-table step was never needed; driver spent

lineage.driver: Members of a pool leave at their own steady rates, which differ widely, so the fast leavers go first and the pool's overall leaving rate falls as its members age; while new members kept arriving the overall rate held high, and once admission stops the closed pool sheds its newest members and then slows, so carrying the open pool's rate overstates the forward losses, and because the record opens part-way through most members' lives, the rate by tenure has to count each member from when the record first sees them.
lineage.architecture: v1 loop 3 (Millrind's 2027 paid moderation pool, nine sites behind a closing volunteer review community, the 2027 pool carried on survival by tenure)
lineage.stump: Carrying each site's reviewer pool from September 2026 at its own lapse rate of the last two years, with no new reviewers since access became invitation-only, files 41 FTE (40 on the last twelve months' rate, 38 on the last three); the step that lands it there is reading one stop rate off a pool that was still taking in newcomers, when reviewers stop at about 9 per cent a month in their first year and under one per cent from their fourth: carried on the stop rate of each reviewer's own tenure, counted from when the roster first sees them, the 10,607 active reviewers average about 8,800 a month in 2027 and the request is 32 FTE (27 with the tenure curve read from each grant date).
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-31 at the batch 1 triage: loop 3 was reshipped 10-27 after the portal's FAILED_TO_STUMP on loops 1 and 2 (both responses filed the then golden), keeping the world, the prompt and the asks the portal had already solved once; re-rooted in a new world before any portal result on loop 3

solved, FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal (2026-10-27): both responses filed 35 FTE, the then golden, by building each site's capacity against its inbox at the saturated pace and carrying each pool at its own lapse rate with almost no new reviewers; the capacity framing was the strong solver's default, so loop 3 moved the decisive step to how the pool is carried
lineage.driver: Work reaches a paid tier only when a volunteer tier falls short, and the volunteer tier's capacity shows only in the periods it fell short, since in every other period it handled everything that arrived; with almost no new volunteers arriving, each pool shrinks at a steady exit rate, so units whose records show almost nothing reaching the paid tier cross below their arrivals inside the forward window, while a share of arrivals carried forward, a trend in the paid work, or capacity read from recent throughput each misses the crossing.
lineage.driver_concrete: Every community review item at Millrind goes first to the volunteer reviewers and reaches the paid moderators only if no volunteer has reviewed it 72 hours after it entered the inbox; volunteers review at their own pace when the inbox is full and below it when it runs dry, so their pace shows only in months when items were routed (most sites in 2022, Security, Embedded & Hardware and Scientific Computing since 2025), and since almost no member has been granted review access after autumn 2024 every site's pool shrinks by about two per cent a month, which takes Data & ML, Databases, Infrastructure & DevOps and Game Development, with almost nothing routed since January 2024, below their 2027 inbox arrivals.
lineage.stump: Carrying each site's paid queue hours per question over the last twelve months onto the 2027 question plan files a request of 23 FTE (25 to 28 with each site's routed share or its monthly paid hours trended forward), inside finance's 26-FTE envelope; the step that lands it there is treating routed items as a share of arrivals, when they are the arrivals each site's shrinking reviewer pool cannot review at the pace reviewers keep when the inbox is full, which puts four sites that have routed almost nothing since January 2024 short of their 2027 inbox and files 35 (31 with the pool trended over the platform's whole record, 53 with the pace read from 2026 throughput).

lineage.niche: a regional public rapid-charging operator in Ireland preparing its concession's 2027 availability plan: which hubs will have a high-power charge point below the 99 per cent contract-year availability standard after the partnership's programme removes the end-of-life 50 kW units at some hubs, when the high-power units' controller hangs, which only an on-site power cycle clears, follow the days since the hub was last powered down
lineage.stakeholder_role: the operator's network performance lead, who prepares the concession's 2027 availability plan for the partnership's annual review

world.geography: Ireland (a fictional operator, partnership and hubs)
world.org_type: regional public rapid-charging operator under a local authority concession

lineage.driver: Each unit's failures run on a clock that its site's other units' repairs reset, so its recorded failure rate is a property of how often those neighbours were repaired, and a forward plan that removes the failing neighbours stops the resets and multiplies the survivors' failures, which every route carried on each unit's own record misses while it validates on the years the resets ran.
lineage.driver_concrete: A high-power charge point's controller hangs only after about 75 days without a power-up, and the legacy 50 kW unit's monthly cabinet service isolates the supply pillar it shares with the high-power units at most hubs, so through 2023 to 2026 the units on a pillar of their own carried 95 of the record's 105 hangs; the partnership's programme removes the legacy units at some hubs in December 2026, after which those hubs are powered down only for planned visits and supply faults and, where visits are twice a year, their high-power units hang two or three times a year, as often as the units on a pillar of their own already do.
lineage.stump: Carrying each high-power charge point's controller-hang and fault rates from 2023 to 2026, validated leaving each unit out and on two back-tests, files only the five hubs whose units already hang; the step that lands it there is reading each unit's hang rate as its own, when a hang comes only after about 75 days without a power-up and the legacy unit's monthly cabinet service powers down every unit on its pillar, so at the seven standard hubs the programme strips the high-power units will run months between power-ups and the set is twelve.
lineage.answer: List 12 hubs in the 2027 Availability Plan: Ballinkeel Main Street, Bunacurry Pier, Carrowkeel Business Park, Clonlea Leisure Centre, Derrylane Park and Ride, Glenfad Shopping Centre, Kilbeg Retail Park, Portavaddy Seafront, Rathmoy Station Road, Rossnabeg Harbour, Tobernalt Road and Tullymore Market Square.
lineage.architecture: v4 (architecture 4: an Irish regional rapid-charging operator's 2027 availability plan, the hubs whose high-power charge points fall below 99 per cent once the renewal programme removes the 50 kW units)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-08 on the platform: both runs landed the golden 12 hubs (the author reports not stumped; no rubric). Both read the hang ages off the first histogram (no hang before day 76 after a power-up), fitted a censored hazard on time since restart with the work orders' power cycles as the remedy, simulated the renewed network and back-tested on 2026; a mechanism the rows carry in one plot, with its remedy written in the work orders, was modelled on sight
